---
title: "Install"
description: "Install Storywell, set up StoryGraph write-back, and register your first source."
---

Storywell is a Python CLI (3.11–3.12). The recommended install is [pipx](https://pipx.pypa.io),
which keeps it in its own isolated environment.

```sh
pipx install storywell
```

## StoryGraph write-back

StoryGraph has no import API, so Storywell writes through a real browser session using
[Playwright](https://playwright.dev/python/). Install the browser once:

```sh
pipx inject storywell playwright
playwright install chromium
```

Then log in a single time — Storywell saves the session and reuses it for every later sync:

```sh
storywell storygraph-login          # opens a browser; log in, then return to the terminal
storywell storygraph-status         # check the saved session is still valid
```

## Register a source

Every sync reads from a `--source` (default: `audible`). List what's available:

```sh
storywell sources
```

### Audible

The Audible source uses [`audible-cli`](https://github.com/mkb79/audible-cli) to register your
account once:

```sh
pipx install audible-cli
audible quickstart
```

Storywell reads `~/.audible/config.toml` to find the active profile's auth file. If you use a
non-default profile, pass `--profile <name>`; to bypass discovery entirely, pass
`--auth-file /path/to/profile.json`.

### File & API sources

Goodreads, Kobo, and LibraryThing read a file you already have; Hardcover reads an API. None
need a separate install — you point Storywell at the export or token at run time. See
[Sources](sources.qmd) for where each input comes from.

## Upgrading from `audible-storygraph-sync`

The project was renamed from `audible-storygraph-sync` to Storywell. The rename moved the config
directory and namespaced sync-store keys under their source. Carry your saved StoryGraph login and
sync history forward once — non-destructively:

```sh
storywell migrate-store
```
